user.title: Connect to UptimeSphere
user.description: Enter the address of your UptimeSphere instance and paste an API token. Create the token in UptimeSphere under “API tokens”.

data_description.base_url: For example https://uptime.example.com — the site root, not a subpage.
data_description.api_token: Create one at /tokens in the UptimeSphere web interface.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn off only if the server uses a self-signed certificate.

reauth_confirm.title: Reauthenticate UptimeSphere
reauth_confirm.description: The API token for {url} is no longer accepted. Create a new one at /tokens and paste it here.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect. Check the address and that the server is reachable from Home Assistant.
error.invalid_auth: The token was rejected. Create a new one at /tokens and paste it here.
error.no_team: The token is valid, but this account currently has no team. Sign in to the UptimeSphere web interface once and select a team.
error.invalid_url: Enter a full address including http:// or https://.
error.invalid_host: That address responded, but not with the UptimeSphere API. Does it point at the instance root?
error.unknown: Unexpected error — see the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: This account is already set up for this UptimeSphere instance.
abort.wrong_account: The token belongs to a different UptimeSphere account.

init.title: UptimeSphere settings
init.description: Detail data (response time, uptime, SSL) is expensive server-side — keep that interval generous.

data_description.notify_service: Leave empty to send no notification. The event is fired either way.

no_team.title: UptimeSphere: no team available
no_team.description: UptimeSphere reports no accessible team for this account. This also happens with a valid API token once the server-side CodeSphere session has expired. Sign in at {url} in a browser once; the integration recovers on its own afterwards.
